claims.text: NbMoTaW and WTaMoNbV are refractory high-entropy alloy systems relevant to extreme-temperature applications.
WTaMoNbV has substantial diversity in the melting points of its constituent elements.
Experimental high-temperature thermodynamic data are sparse or unreliable for the targeted refractory alloys.
A framework combining an MLIP trained on sparse high-temperature AIMD data with an elemental-melting-point-variance correction can accurately predict RHEA melting properties.
Training the MLIP specifically on liquid-phase and melting-transition AIMD configurations will make it suitable for predicting melting behavior.
A thermodynamic correction can be derived from the variance of the constituent elemental melting points.
Lennard-Jones potentials alone are unreliable for predicting multicomponent HEA behavior.
Classical potentials fail because they cannot represent complex multicomponent electronic interactions and directional bonding at high temperatures.
CALPHAD predictions for high-temperature HEAs are limited by incomplete or inaccurate thermodynamic databases.
SOAP or ACSF local-environment descriptors capture short-range order and lattice distortion in RHEA liquids.
Simple mixing rules and Lennard-Jones potentials do not account for the relevant liquid short-range order and lattice-distortion effects.
The proposed MLIP will capture local structural distortions and electronic effects in the liquid state.
Differences among constituent elemental melting points produce thermodynamic driving-force differences that can be represented by the proposed correction term.
Combining the MLIP and correction term will permit accurate extrapolation without extensive experimental calibration.
The framework will predict melting temperatures within 5% of experimental values.
The framework will provide reliable entropy-of-fusion and liquid heat-capacity estimates for untested RHEA compositions.
The framework will outperform pure CALPHAD and classical molecular dynamics.
The method is valid for substitutional solid-solution refractory alloys where high-entropy theory applies.

The method will fail or require substantial retraining for systems with large formation heats that promote oxide, carbide, or nitride formation, or for liquids with unrepresented extreme chemical ordering.
Interatomic-potential transferability at high temperatures and outside the training composition space requires further validation.

contradictions.description: The proposed framework is defined as an MLIP plus an elemental-melting-point-variance correction, but the falsification design calls it an 'MLIP-CALPHAD' framework. It is therefore unclear whether CALPHAD is part of the intervention or merely a baseline.
